concept.title: How a Home Network Works?
concept.shortdesc: A home network enables connected devices to communicate with each other and access Internet services through a router and an Internet connection provided by an Internet Service Provider (ISP).

section.title: Overview
section.p: A home network consists of devices that are connected through wired or wireless connections. These devices communicate through a central networking device, such as the .
The receives Internet connectivity from the and provides network access to connected devices.

section.title: Communication Flow
section.p: When a device sends a request to access an Internet resource, the request passes through the home network before it reaches the destination.
The manages data traffic between the local network and the Internet.

section.title: Data Exchange Between Devices
section.p: Devices on the same home network can communicate directly with each other through the .
For example, a laptop can send data to a printer, or a smart TV can access media stored on a network storage device.
This communication occurs within the local network and does not require Internet access.

section.title: Wired and Wireless Connectivity
section.p: Devices can connect to the home network through Ethernet connections or Wi Fi connections.
Wired devices connect to an available on the .
Wireless devices connect to the Wi Fi network identified by the SSID .

section.title: Role of the Router
section.p: The serves as the central device in the home network.
The router connects devices, manages network traffic, and provides access to Internet resources.
The router also maintains communication between wired and wireless devices on the network.
